transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start: 15:00 PDT (UTC-7)
Duration: 42 minutes
Title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Nexus Payments
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Nexus Head of Platform), Lisa Wu (Nexus VP Eng), Ravi Patel (Nexus SRE), Alyssa Chen (Nexus Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick renewal conversation + proposal for additional capacity and new regions, security docs requested, timeline for contract amendment discussed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh we wanted to run through renewal and expansion options for Nexus, check what you've seen in the usage spike, and next steps to lock in the dedicated pools.
[00:20] Carlos Mendez: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. yeah we've seen a big ramp with the new checkout flows, throughput's up about 3x month over month. so want to make sure we don't get throttled during peak.
[00:34] Samira Khan: got it, and congrats on that growth — quick question, that 3x, is that sustained or spiky around marketing pushes?
[00:42] Lisa Wu: mostly pushes, but baseline went up too. it's a mix, i'd say ~60% sustained higher baseline and the rest are spikes.
[00:50] Ravi Patel: the SRE side is concerned about cold starts and the latency tail. we're seeing occasional p95 spikes to ~650ms on hosted, which is fine but we want headroom.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: understood. so couple levers we mentioned in the deck — dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), region expansion so traffic is routed closer to users, and some batching/kv cache tuning.
[01:18] Carlos Mendez: can you remind us the delta in unit cost between hosted and dedicated? last call was fuzzy on the numbers.
[01:26] Jordan Lee: sure, roughly speaking hosted is pay-as-you-go — if you keep current patterns you'd pay about X per 1M tokens, dedicated has a fixed commit but reduces unit cost by around 30-45% depending on utilization. i'll send the updated tiered pricing in the follow up.
[01:42] Lisa Wu: that 30-45% range depends on utilization, right? if we underutilize we might pay more.
[01:48] Samira Khan: exactly, that's why we recommend a sizing workshop — we run projected QPS + sequence length distribution, and show committed tiers that map to your historical and forecasted load.
[02:02] Alyssa Chen: procurement question — how does contract term affect price? do we need annual to get reserved pricing?
[02:08] Jordan Lee: generally annual or 12-month commitments unlock the better pricing. we can do short term pilots on hosted while we size the dedicated commit.
[02:18] Carlos Mendez: region ask — we have increasing traffic in EU and APAC. can Redwood support eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 for private deployments?
[02:28] Samira Khan: yes, we support those regions. for Private (V P C) we can spin up control plane in your VPC or provide a managed private offering, you'll want to decide on data residency and KMS.
[02:42] Ravi Patel: on KMS, we use an HSM-backed key for token encryption — do you integrate with customer KMS or is it service-managed?
[02:50] Samira Khan: we support customer-managed KMS for private and dedicated options, and HSM-backed keys for enterprises. we'll share the security pack with details — includes S S O, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and SOC 2 artifacts.
[03:05] Lisa Wu: perfect, please include retention and log export formats in that pack.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: noted.
[03:16] Carlos Mendez: on the expansion, what about fallbacks if a region hits capacity — can traffic route automatically to a secondary region or a cheaper model?
[03:26] Samira Khan: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallbacks — policies can be set for latency SLOs or cost thresholds. for example route to a compatible quantized variant or another region.
[03:38] Ravi Patel: any concerns around model compatibility if we fallback to a different variant? we don't want behavior drift.
[03:45] Samira Khan: good point — we recommend testing with eval prompt sets in both variants. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions and we can keep canary routing for gradual rollouts.
[03:58] Lisa Wu: timeline question — we're hoping to have committed capacity in place before our Q3 launch mid-July. is that feasible?
[04:06] Jordan Lee: yes, if we finalize numbers and sign by early June we can provision dedicated pools and start migration in June/early July. provisioning lead time depends on GPU availability but we can do a phased rollout.
[04:18] Alyssa Chen: procurement — to sign early June we need a contract amendment and PO. what's typical cycle time?
[04:24] Jordan Lee: usually 2–3 weeks for the contract amendment plus PO processing on your side; we'll draft the amendment and rate table.
[04:32] Alyssa Chen: ok that timeline aligns if we act quickly.
[04:36] Carlos Mendez: technical deep dive — Samira, can you walk through the sizing factors you need from us? CPU/GPU usage is obvious but what else?
[04:44] Samira Khan: primarily historic QPS, average and p95 sequence lengths, concurrency, and traffic distribution by region. also retry patterns and any long-context calls that hold KV cache. if you have trace spans showing distribution that helps.
[05:00] Ravi Patel: we can pull those metrics from our telemetry, i'll include a sample dataset in the sizing workshop.
[05:06] Samira Khan: perfect. also any constraints on outbound egress or private peering? that affects the private deployment topology.
[05:14] Carlos Mendez: we have existing private peering with our cloud provider and an internal firewall policy, so we prefer V P C peering.
[05:21] Jordan Lee: makes sense. we'll include a migration runbook for the peering setup and test plan.
[05:28] Lisa Wu: question on quality — Nexus uses the model for regulatory language and disclaimers, so accuracy/regressions are a high bar for us. can Redwood commit to quality monitoring?
[05:36] Samira Khan: yes, Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. we can set thresholds and trigger rollback or alerting.
[05:43] Carlos Mendez: great. can you also include a sample SLA for p95 tail? we've had customer-facing incidents when that slips.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: we'll include the SLA language in the amendment; dedicated capacity has SLA options with credits.
[05:56] Ravi Patel: about benchmarks — last time we ran an internal comparison some results differed because of sequence padding. any guidance to reproduce your numbers?
[06:04] Samira Khan: yep, we'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and best practices — sequence bucketing, warm KV cache versus cold starts, and perf flags. those notes will be in the security/ops pack.
[06:18] Alyssa Chen: procurement detail — do you require invoice-based billing or card? we prefer invoiced for enterprise.
[06:24] Jordan Lee: invoiced billing on net-30 is standard for enterprise; we can support PO-based billing.
[06:29] Carlos Mendez: ok let's talk expand numbers — we're looking at a 2x reserved capacity compared to current commit, plus two additional regions. what's the incremental cost and lead time?
[06:40] Samira Khan: incremental cost depends on GPU type and utilization; i'll model 2x on the same instance families and include region replication costs. lead time for region activation is generally 2–4 weeks once contracts are signed and capacity ordered.
[06:53] Lisa Wu: are multi-region active-active setups supported? we want low latency in both EU and APAC simultaneously.
[06:59] Samira Khan: yes, active-active is supported, we just need routing rules and failover policies; note that cross-region replication for KV cache is eventual so warm-up is needed.
[07:12] Ravi Patel: any special compliance for EU? data residency, GDPR, and local logging?
[07:17] Samira Khan: we support EU data residency and local log retention — audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. all in the pack.
[07:26] Jordan Lee: to keep this practical I propose these immediate next steps: Jordan sends updated pricing & contract amendment, Samira runs sizing and shares a proposed committed tier and slide deck, Samira also shares security pack, Nexus confirms regions and internal timelines, Procurement checks PO and signature timelines.
[07:43] Carlos Mendez: that works. one more question — any hidden fees for burst capacity? sometimes vendors charge extra when we exceed commit.
[07:52] Jordan Lee: we have burst policies — you can have capped burst with an agreed overage rate; we'll put that in the amendment so it's transparent.
[07:59] Lisa Wu: excellent. any competitors we should be aware of — we've been evaluating OpenAI and Anthropic as well.
[08:06] Jordan Lee: understood, we'll include a short doc comparing tradeoffs — cost, latency, and enterprise controls.
[08:12] Alyssa Chen: procurement will want to see the SLA and security pack before PO.
[08:16] Jordan Lee: we'll prioritize sharing those within 48 hours.
[08:20] Carlos Mendez: okay timeline consensus: Jordan by 5/5 for pricing, Samira sizing by 5/6, Nexus confirm regions by 5/8, procurement reply by 5/7.
[08:30] Samira Khan: I'll also include a proposed migration window and a test plan for the Q3 launch.
[08:36] Ravi Patel: sounds good. small nit — sometimes the transcript names your product names wrong in our logs, what is Redwood's private offering called again?
[08:44] Jordan Lee: Redwood Private, sometimes folks say "Redwood Private V P C" or just "Private".
[08:48] Lisa Wu: perfect. thanks everyone.
[08:50] Jordan Lee: thanks all — we'll follow up. Jordan out.
